rituals.name: PATTERN MAGNET
rituals.plain:
Two striking things happened together. Your brain may be exaggerating the romance.
Use four cases: A+calm, A+tense, B+calm, B+tense—one of each. First notice any intuitive group-feeling link, then count the actual pairings.

rituals.name: POINT-OF-NO-RETURN

Where does this habit become a real commitment? Not every step is a signed contract.
Take one harmless habit. Mentally list its first few physical microsteps—reach, pick up, open, move—and find the earliest step that makes continuation noticeably harder to reverse.
Describe physical steps, not intentions.
Move your intervention point one step earlier than that commitment point.

rituals.name: MEANS DISTANCE
rituals.plain:
SUPPORT FIRST
MEANS DISTANCE

WHAT'S HAPPENING
[USER THOUGHT]

DO NOW
If risk is meaningful, move yourself or the means farther apart and involve another person.

NEXT
No inward experiment substitutes for this.

WHY THIS MATTERS
Access to action becomes harder in the real environment.

REMEMBER
Increasing distance from harmful means changes which actions are immediately available; safety can therefore be built into the physical choice architecture.

SAFETY
This is not an inward coping test: if harmful action is a real possibility, increase physical distance from the means now and involve a trusted person, clinician, crisis service, or emergency support as appropriate.

rituals.name: EASY-ANSWER TRAP

Harder recall can feel like worse evidence. Effort isn't an honesty rating.
Think of three reasons you could handle a presentation. Notice confidence. Then try to generate eight reasons and notice confidence again, including how hard the list became.
Use the same topic for both rounds.
Don't treat list length alone as the answer; notice retrieval ease.

rituals.name: MOTOR-TIME MIRROR

Choose a safe action such as touching thumb to each fingertip in sequence. First imagine one complete sequence and count its duration; then perform it once at a natural pace and compare.
Use the identical movement in imagination and reality.
Don't deliberately speed up or slow down the real movement.

rituals.name: SECOND-TARGET BLIND
rituals.plain:
Two targets arrive close together. Attention has a tiny blind beat.
Run mentally: A, 4, C, 7, F, G, H. Afterward report both digits without replaying the stream.
Read the sequence once at roughly one item per quick beat.
Then repeat with A, 4, C, D, E, 7, H and compare the second-target catch.

rituals.thought_engineering_mechanism: Urge–action decoupling via add one practical step between urge and target behavior: let the thought generate pressure while inserting a distinct cognitive boundary before behaviour.
rituals.optional_check_in: Any more room to choose your next move, or not yet?
